findings.title: Mixed JSON encoding still disguises reserved storage content
findings.detail: In an independent isolated Git fixture, prefixing a UTF-32LE gzip-v1 JSON body with a UTF-16LE BOM causes json.detect_encoding to select UTF-16, after which decoding produces interleaved NUL characters and the marker prefilter returns None. With the named gzip payload removed, read returns the malformed envelope bytes as plain evidence, evidence_exists accepts the blob even with wrong expected command and exit code, and the prospective audit reports errors=[]. Malformed reserved encoding therefore still bypasses availability, payload integrity and metadata binding, contrary to EVIDENCE_STORAGE_POLICY.
findings.requested_change: Recognize or reject malformed reserved storage content despite conflicting BOM/body encodings before permitting plain fallback. Preserve unrelated opaque historical bytes and add focused mixed-BOM/encoding missing-payload and metadata-binding negatives across read, availability and audit; rerun independent reviews on the corrected revision.
